title: Artist Statement
body:
In My Room - Installation and ceramic exhibition at Tennessee Gallery

In this body of work, I have created an installation of ceramic relief sculptures that use the formal elements of drawing (line, shape, space, form, texture) to create a large-scale composition based on the drawings that I do in my sketchbook. Using ceramic relief sculptures as elements in an installation of a drawing composition brings a more substantial and tactile layer of depth to my work.

I intentionally developed the characters based on my personal life, using them as compositional elements to express the collision of beauty, delight, chaos, and the mundane that is present in my day to day. It becomes a form of theater—a direct view into my imagination.

The title of this show "In My Room" is a nod to Virginia Woolf's “A Room of One's Own“. I am placing my work in the context of being made from a feminine perspective but also making room for an androgynous point of view. While I believe my work could be viewed as distinctly feminine, it treats that perspective with a certain indifference, focusing instead on creation for its own sake: me creating for me regardless of my identity. There are 3 rooms present in this exhibition. The work is placed within the gallery room, creates a room of its own through drawing perspective tools and has a room drawn on the pedestal that the woman is on. It makes the installation self aware and infinite. It looks at itself and expands and contracts the ideas presented within the installation.

CERAMIC SCULPTOR / VISUAL ARTIST

I am currently exploring the intersection of Drawing and Sculpture by developing ceramic relief sculptures that use the formal elements of drawing (line, shape, space, form, texture) and the tactile and weighty properties of clay to create a large-scale “Room” installations based off of my drawings that express the messy mix of life: beauty, delight, chaos, and the mundane.
